\[R\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^n(D), \mathbb{Z}/\ell) = \mathbb{Z}/\ell \text{ placed in degree 0} \, .\]
The \(H^i\) of the two sides of 5.5.28.1 are therefore zero, and the arrow induced on \(H^0\) is identified with the identity of \(\mathbb{Z}/\ell\).
5.5.29. For the application we have in view, it is useful to regard a quasi-coherent sheaf on a scheme \(X\) as a quasi-coherent sheaf of \(\mathcal{O}\)-modules on the étale site of \(X\).
Let \(p : X \longrightarrow S\) be a quasi-projective morphism of schemes (cf. 5.5.21.1(∗)). If \(F\) is a sheaf of \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules on \(X_{\mathrm{ét}}\), then

a) We denote by \(\otimes^n F\) the sheaf of modules on \((X/S)^n_{\mathrm{ét}}\) which is the tensor product of the \(\mathcal{O}_{(X/S)^n}\)-modules, \(n\) in number, that are the inverse images of \(F\) on \((X/S)^n_{\mathrm{ét}}\);

b) the sheaf \(\otimes^n F\) is an \(\mathfrak{S}_n\)-equivariant sheaf. By passage to the invariants, it defines a sheaf \(\mathrm{TS}^n_{\mathrm{ext}}(F)\) on \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)\): if \(\sigma\) is the projection of \((X/S)^n\) onto \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)\), we have
\[(5.5.29.1) \qquad \mathrm{TS}^n_{\mathrm{ext}}(F) = (\sigma_* \otimes^n F)^{\mathfrak{S}_n} \, .\]

Suppose that \(p\) is flat; as in 5.5.8, we then define the functor \(\Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}}\) as the \(0\)-th left derived functor of the functor \(\mathrm{TS}^n_{\mathrm{ext}}\). With the notation of 5.5.2.5 and 5.5.8, if
\[P_1 \longrightarrow P_0 \longrightarrow F \longrightarrow 0\]
is a flat presentation of \(F\), then the sequence
\[\mathrm{TS}^n_{\mathrm{ext}}(P'_1) \overset{j_0}{\underset{j_1}{\rightrightarrows}} \mathrm{TS}^n_{\mathrm{ext}}(P_0) \longrightarrow \Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}}(F)\]
is exact. If \(x\) is a geometric point of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)\) as in 5.5.7.1, we have (cf. 5.5.8.1)

\[(5.5.29.2) \qquad \Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}}(F)_x = \mathcal{O}_x \otimes_C \Bigl( \bigotimes_1^\ell \Gamma^{n_i}_{\mathcal{O}_S}(F_{y_i}) \Bigr) \, , \quad \text{with} \quad C = \bigotimes_1^\ell \operatorname{Sym}^{n_i}_{\mathcal{O}_S}(\mathcal{O}_{y_i}) \, .\]

It indeed suffices to verify this formula in the trivial case where the fibres of \(F\) are free. Note that \(\mathcal{O}_x\) is flat over \(C\), being the strict henselization of \(C\) at the closed point image of \(x\).

5.5.30. Suppose \(X\) and \(S\) affine, \(p\) flat and \(F\) quasi-coherent. Let \(S = \operatorname{Spec}(A)\), \(X = \operatorname{Spec}(B)\) and let \(F = H^0(X, F)\), so that \(F\) is the sheaf \(\widetilde{F}\) defined by the \(B\)-module \(F\). We then read off from (5.5.29.1) that
\[\mathrm{TS}^n_{\mathrm{ext}}(F) = \widetilde{\mathrm{TS}^n_A(F)} \, ,\]
and, by derivation, we therefore have
\[(5.5.30.1) \qquad \Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}}(F) = \widetilde{\Gamma^n_A(F)} \, .\]
The functor \(\Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}}\) thus appears as a functor \(\Gamma^n\) "relative to \(A\)", which (5.5.29.2) already expressed in local form.

5.5.31. We shall denote by \(D^{b,\mathrm{tor}_S \leq 0}(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\) the subcategory of \(D^b(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\) consisting of the complexes of \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules which, as complexes of \(p^{-1}(\mathcal{O}_S)\)-modules, are of Tor-dimension \(\leq 0\).
Consider the condition

(5.5.31.1) \(K \in \operatorname{Ob} C^{b,\geq 0}(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\) and, at each geometric point \(x\) of \(X\), \(K_x\) is homotopic to a complex of \(\mathcal{O}_{X,x}\)-modules, in positive degrees, flat over \(\mathcal{O}_{S,p(x)}\).

Since the morphism \(p\) is flat, so that there are "enough" \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules flat over \(S\), one verifies as in 5.5.13.2 that \(D^{b,\mathrm{tor}_S \leq 0}(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\) is obtained from the category of complexes \(K \in \operatorname{Ob} K^{b,\geq 0}(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\) satisfying (5.5.31.1) by inverting the quasi-isomorphisms.

One reads off from (5.5.29.2) and 5.5.6.1 that if \(u : K \longrightarrow L\) is a quasi-isomorphism between complexes satisfying (5.5.31.1), then \(\Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}}(u)\) (in the sense of DOLD-PUPPE) is again a quasi-isomorphism. The functor \(\Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}}\) is therefore derived into

\[(5.5.31.2) \qquad L\Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}} : D^{b,\mathrm{tor}_S \leq 0}(X, \mathcal{O}_X) \longrightarrow D^{b,\mathrm{tor}_S \leq 0}(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X), \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)})\]

5.5.32. We shall denote by \(D^{b,\mathrm{tor}_S \leq 0}_{\mathrm{qcoh}}(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\) the subcategory of \(D^{b,\mathrm{tor}_S \leq 0}(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\) consisting of the complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology.
Standard arguments allow us, as in 5.5.17, to define a symmetric Künneth arrow of the following type:

Let \(u : X \longrightarrow Y\) be a morphism of \(S\)-schemes quasi-projective and flat over \(S\); for \(K \in \operatorname{Ob} D^{b,\mathrm{tor}_S \leq 0}_{\mathrm{qcoh}}(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\), the symmetric Künneth arrow \(k^n\) in \(D^{b,\mathrm{tor}_S \leq 0}_{\mathrm{qcoh}}(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(Y), \mathcal{O})\) is an arrow
\[(5.5.32.1) \qquad k^n : L\Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}} Ru_*K \longrightarrow R\operatorname{Sym}^n_S u_* L\Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}} K \, .\]
We leave to the reader the task of verifying the formal properties of 5.5.32.1 that will be used, in particular the following one:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 5.5.33

If \(S\) is of characteristic \(p > 0\), and if \(u : X \longrightarrow S\) is proper and flat, the diagram of symmetric Künneth arrows 5.5.17.2 and 5.5.32.1 is commutative (\(Y = S\), \(K = \mathbb{Z}/p\) or \(\mathcal{O}_X\)) :

\[\xymatrix@C=4em@R=3.5em{ L\Gamma^n_{\mathbb{Z}/p} Ru_*(\mathbb{Z}/p) \ar[r]^-{k^n} \ar[d] & R\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(u)_*(\mathbb{Z}/p) \ar[d] \\ L\Gamma^n_{\mathcal{O}} Ru_*(\mathcal{O}) \ar[r]_-{k^n} & R\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(u)_*(\mathcal{O}) } \, .\]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 5.5.34

Under the hypotheses of 5.5.32, the symmetric Künneth arrow (5.5.32.1) is an isomorphism.
a) The question is local on \(S\), which we may assume to be affine.

b) For every point \(x\) of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(Y)\), there exists an affine open subset \(Y_1\) of \(Y\) such that \(x\) lies in \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(Y_1)\). By localization, we may therefore assume \(Y\) affine.

c) Every complex \(K\) of the type considered can be represented by a complex \(K_0\) of quasi-coherent modules on \(S\), zero in degrees \(i < 0\). If \(\mathcal{U}\) is an affine covering of \(X\), then \(K\) admits a finite resolution by sums of complexes of the form \(j_* j^*K\) for \(j\) the inclusion of an affine open subset (alternating Čech complex). Using the quasi-coherent analogue of the dévissage lemma 5.5.22.2, this reduces us to the case where there exists an affine open subset \(j : X_1 \longrightarrow X\) of \(X\) and \(K_1 \in D^{b,\mathrm{tor}_S \leq 0}_{\mathrm{qcoh}}(X_1, \mathcal{O})\) such that \(K = Rj_* K_1\).

d) In view of the quasi-coherent analogue of the transitivity 5.5.20.2, it suffices to prove 5.5.34 for \(uj\) and \(j\). The reduction b), applied to \(j\), finally reduces us to the case where \(X\), \(Y\) and \(S\) are affine. We can then represent \(K\) by a complex \(K_2 \in C^{b,\geq 0}(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\) with flat quasi-coherent components ( ). The functors \(Ru_*\) and \(L\Gamma^n\) are then computed without any further need to resolve \(K_2\), and it remains to note that, by 5.5.30.1, for \(F\) quasi-coherent on \(X\), we have
\[\Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}} u_* F \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(u)_* \Gamma^n_{\mathrm{ext}} F \, ,\]
both sides being identified with
\[\widetilde{\Gamma^n_A(F)} \quad \text{for } F = \widetilde{F} \, ,\]
qed.
5.5.35. Let us treat case 2 of 5.5.26. With the notation of 5.5.22, the following diagram is commutative (5.5.33):

\[(5.5.35.1) \qquad \xymatrix@C=4em@R=3.5em{ L\Gamma^n(R\Gamma(X, \mathbb{Z}/p)) \ar[r]^-{k^n}_-{\text{①}} \ar[d] & R\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^n_k(X), \mathbb{Z}/p) \ar[d] \\ L\Gamma^n(R\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O})) \ar[r]^-{k^n}_-{\text{②}} & R\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^n_k(X), \mathcal{O}) } \, ,\]

and by 5.5.34, the arrow ② is an isomorphism. The Frobenius endomorphism \(F : x \longrightarrow x^p\) of \(\mathcal{O}\) acts \(p\)-linearly on \(R\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O})\) and on \(R\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^n_k(X), \mathcal{O})\). It therefore also acts \(p\)-linearly on \(L\Gamma^n(R\Gamma(X,\mathcal{O}))\). One verifies that \(k^n\) and \(F\) commute.
Artin-Schreier theory provides us with exact sequences
\[0 \longrightarrow H^i(X, \mathbb{Z}/p) \longrightarrow H^i(X, \mathcal{O}) \xrightarrow{\;F-I\;} H^i(X, \mathcal{O}) \longrightarrow 0 \, ,\]
and similarly for \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)\). To deduce that ① is an isomorphism from the fact that ② is one, it remains for us to verify the

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 5.5.36

Let \(k\) be a perfect field of characteristic \(p > 0\), \(K \in C^{\geq 0}(\mathbb{Z}/p)\) a complex of finite-dimensional \(\mathbb{Z}/p\)-vector spaces, \(L \in C^{\geq 0}(k)\) a complex of finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector spaces, \(F\) a \(p\)-linear endomorphism of \(L\) and \(u : K \longrightarrow L\) a morphism. Suppose that \(H^*(Fu) = H^*(u)\), and that the sequences

\[0 \longrightarrow H^i(K) \longrightarrow H^i(L) \xrightarrow{\;F-I\;} H^i(L) \longrightarrow 0\]

are exact. Then, the sequences

\[0 \longrightarrow H^i(\Gamma^n K) \longrightarrow H^i(\Gamma^n L) \xrightarrow{\;F-I\;} H^i(\Gamma^n L) \longrightarrow 0\]

are exact.
Since \(H^*(Fu) = H^*(u)\) and \(\mathbb{Z}/p\) is a field, there exists a homotopy
Since the field \(k\) is perfect, we can write
Replacing \(u\) by \(u - (dH_0 + H_0 d)\), we may assume that \(Fu = u\).

The functor \(S\) that associates to each \(k\)-vector space \(V\) equipped with a \(p\)-linear endomorphism \(F\) the \(\mathbb{Z}/p\)-vector space \(V^S\) of the \(v \in V\) such that \(Fv = v\) is an exact functor. The hypothesis therefore means that the morphism
\[K \longrightarrow L^S\]

is a quasi-isomorphism. It remains to prove that the functor \(S\) commutes with the functor \(\Gamma^n\). This point follows easily from the following well-known lemma, whose proof is left to the reader:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 5.5.37

A finite-dimensional vector space \(V\) over a perfect field \(k\), equipped with a \(p\)-linear endomorphism \(F\), admits one and only one decomposition

\[V = V_0 + V_n\]

with \(V^S \otimes k \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} V_0\), \(F(V_n) \subset V_n\) and \(F|_{V_n}\) nilpotent.
This completes the proof of 5.5.21.

footnotes.html: (∗) But not in that of Sets!

(∗) Everything that follows, including 5.5.34, is valid assuming only that \(X\) and \(Y\) admit ample invertible sheaves relatively to \(S\) (without assuming \(X\) and \(Y\) of finite type over \(S\)).

blocks.html: 6. The functor \(f_!\).

We propose to give a direct construction of the functor \(f_!\) of 5.1.11. We shall then use this construction to define the "trace morphism" (6.2.3) for flat quasi-finite morphisms of finite presentation.
6.1. New construction of the functor \(f_!\).
Let \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) be a morphism locally of finite type. A subset \(P\) of \(X\) is said to be proper over \(S\) if it is the image of a subscheme of \(X\) proper over \(S\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.1.1

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) be a morphism locally of finite type and quasi-separated.

(i) A subset of \(X\) proper over \(S\) is locally closed, and is closed if \(f\) is separated.

(ii) If \(f\) is separated, the union of two subsets of \(X\) proper over \(S\) is proper over \(S\).

(iii) For every \(S\)-scheme \(U\), denote by \(\varphi_X(U)\) the set of subsets of \(U \times_S X\) proper over \(U\). The functor \(\varphi_X\) is a sheaf for the fpqc topology. If \(f\) is separated, \(\varphi\) is a sheaf of filtered ordered sets for the inclusion relation.

Assertions (i) and (ii) are trivial, and the second assertion of (iii) follows from (ii). The functor \(U \longmapsto \mathfrak{P}(U \times_S X)\) is a sheaf for every topology for which the coverings are surjective. It follows from EGA IV 2.3.14 and EGA IV 2.7.1 (vii) that \(\varphi_X\) is a subsheaf of it.

If \(\mathfrak{F}\) is an étale sheaf of pointed sets on a scheme \(X\), recall (IV 8.5.2) that the support of a section \(s\) of \(\mathfrak{F}\) is the complement of the largest open subset where \(s = 0\), \(0\) denoting the marked section.

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.html:
Definition 6.1.2

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) be a morphism locally of finite type and separated, and \(\mathfrak{F}\) a sheaf of pointed sets on \(X\). We denote by \(f_! \mathfrak{F}\) the subsheaf of \(f_* \mathfrak{F}\) whose sections over \(U\) (étale over \(S\)) are the sections of \(\mathfrak{F}\) over \(U \times_S X\) with support proper over \(U\).
It follows from 6.1.1 that \(f_! \mathfrak{F}\) is indeed a sheaf.
One easily verifies that:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 6.1.3

If \(f\) is the composite \(g h\) of two separated morphisms locally of finite type, there exists one and only one functor isomorphism \(f_! \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} g_! h_!\) making the diagram commutative
\[\xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=2.4em{ f_! \ar[r]^-{\sim} \ar[d] & g_! h_! \ar[d] \\ f_* \ar@{=}[r] & g_* h_* }\]

If \(f\) is an open immersion (resp. a proper morphism), the functor \(f_!\) is the extension-by-zero functor (resp. the functor \(f_*\)). By 6.1.3, the definitions 6.1.2 and 5.1.11 therefore coincide in their common domain of validity.
The properties of the functor \(f_!\) verified in § 5 remain valid in the more general case 6.1.2.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.1.4

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) be a separated morphism locally of finite type.

(i) The functor \(f_!\) is left exact (i.e. commutes with finite projective limits) and commutes with filtered inductive limits.

(ii) If \(f\) is quasi-finite, the functor \(f_!\) is an exact functor from the category of abelian sheaves on \(X\) to that of abelian sheaves on \(S\).

(iii) For every cartesian diagram

\[\xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=2em{ X' \ar[r]^{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^{f} \\ S' \ar[r]_{g} & S }\]

there exists a base-change isomorphism making the diagram commutative

\[\xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=2.4em{ g^*f_! \ar@{=}[r] \ar[d] & f'_! g'^* \ar[d] \\ g^*f_* \ar[r] & f'_* g'^* }\]

in which the second horizontal arrow is the base-change arrow XII 4.1.
Proof. For every \(U \in \operatorname{Ob} S_{\mathrm{ét}}\), we have
\[f_! \mathfrak{F}(U) = \varinjlim_{P \in \varphi(U)} \Gamma_P(\mathfrak{F}) \, ,\]

and for \(U\) quasi-compact quasi-separated, the functor \(\mathfrak{F} \longmapsto f_! \mathfrak{F}(U)\) commutes with finite projective limits and with filtered inductive limits, being a filtered inductive limit (6.1.1) (iii) of functors having these properties.
This proves (i). Assertion (ii) follows immediately from (iii) (take as base changes the geometric points of \(S\)).

Assertion (iii) is local in nature on \(S\), which we may assume to be affine. Let \(I\) be the filtered ordered set of open subsets of \(X\) of finite type over \(S\). If \(U \xrightarrow{\;j\;} X\) is an open subset of \(X\), \((fj)_!(\mathfrak{F}|U) = f_!(j_!(\mathfrak{F}|U))\) maps into \(f_!(\mathfrak{F})\). Moreover
\[f_!(\mathfrak{F}) = \varinjlim_{U \in I} (fj)_!(\mathfrak{F}|U) \, .\]

This allows us to assume \(X\) of finite type over \(S\) and to apply Chow's lemma (EGA II 2nd ed. ) to find a projective surjective morphism \(p^0 : X^0 \longrightarrow X\) such that \(f p^0\) is compactifiable. Let \(X^1 = X^0 \times_X X^0\) and \(p^1\) the natural arrow from \(X^1\) to \(X\). The sequence
\[0 \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F} \longrightarrow p^0_* p^{0*}\mathfrak{F} \rightrightarrows p^1_* p^{1*}\mathfrak{F}\]
is exact (VII 9.2).

Taking into account the functoriality of the base-change arrow, and (i), it suffices to verify (iii) for the sheaves \(p^0_* p^{0*}\mathfrak{F}\) and \(p^1_* p^{1*}\mathfrak{F}\). By the change of notation (\(p^1 \longmapsto p^0\)) we thus reduce to assuming \(\mathfrak{F}\) of the form \(p^0_* \mathfrak{G}\). Assertion (iii) for the pair \((f, p^0_* \mathfrak{G})\) is equivalent to assertion (iii) for the pairs \((p^0, \mathfrak{G})\) and \((f p^0, \mathfrak{G})\). We conclude by 5.2.7 (i), applicable since \(p^0\) and \(fp^0\) are compactifiable.

blocks.title: Counterexample
blocks.html:
Counterexample 6.1.6

The functor \(Rf_!\) does not in general coincide with the derived functor of the functor \(f_!\).
If \(X\) is affine over an algebraically closed field \(k\), we indeed have
\[f_! \mathfrak{F} = \sum_{x \in X(k)} H^0_x(\mathfrak{F}) \, ,\]
and the \(i^{\text{th}}\) derived functor of \(f_!\) therefore equals, at \(\mathfrak{F}\),
\[\sum_{x \in X(k)} H^i_x(\mathfrak{F}) \, .\]
On the other hand, if \(X\) is smooth and irreducible, and of dimension 1,
\[H^2_c(X, \mu_{\ell^n}) \simeq \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n\]
for \(\ell\) prime to the characteristic of \(k\).
6.2. The trace morphism in relative dimension 0.

The main result of this n° is Theorem 6.2.3. The reader is advised not to read the technical preliminaries 6.2.1, 6.2.2. These allow one, in the proof of 6.2.3, to consider only finite morphisms \(f\), a reduction which, via EGA IV 18.12, is in any case fairly obvious.

6.2.1. Let \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) be a quasi-finite separated morphism. For every \(U \in \operatorname{Ob} S_{\mathrm{ét}}\), denote by \(\psi_f(U)\) the category of pairs consisting of a finite pointed set \(I\), with marked point denoted \(0\), and a decomposition of \(f^*U\) into open and closed subsets \(f^*U = \coprod_{i \in I} V_i\), with \(V_i\) finite over \(U\) for \(i \neq 0\). A morphism from \(\varphi = (V_i)_{i \in I}\) to \(\varphi' = (V'_i)_{i \in I'}\) is a morphism \(\sigma\) from \(I'\) to \(I\) such that for \(i \in I\), we have \(V_i = \bigcup_{j \in \sigma^{-1}(i)} V'_j\). We say that \(\varphi'\) refines \(\varphi\) if there exists a morphism from \(\varphi\) to \(\varphi'\).

Let \(\mathfrak{F}\) be a sheaf of abelian groups on \(S\), \(U \in \operatorname{Ob} S_{\mathrm{ét}}\), \(\varphi = (V_i)_{i \in I} \in \operatorname{Ob} \psi_f(U)\), \(I^* = I \setminus \{0\}\), and \(f_i\) the projection of \(V_i\) onto \(U\). We have
\[f_! f^* \mathfrak{F}|U = f_{0!} f_0^*(\mathfrak{F}|U) \oplus \bigoplus_{i \neq 0} f_{i*} f_i^*(\mathfrak{F}|U) \, ,\]
whence a composite arrow
\[(6.2.1.1) \qquad \tau_\varphi : \mathfrak{F}^{I^*}|U \longrightarrow \bigoplus_{i \neq 0} f_{i*} f_i^*(\mathfrak{F}|U) \longrightarrow f_! f^* \mathfrak{F}|U \, .\]

If \(\sigma : I \longrightarrow J\) is a morphism of pointed sets, we denote by \(t_\sigma : \mathfrak{F}^{J^*} \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}^{I^*}\) the arrow with coordinates \(t_\sigma^i = \operatorname{Id}\) if \(\sigma(i) = j\), and \(t_\sigma^i = 0\) if \(\sigma(i) \neq j\). If \(\sigma : I' \longrightarrow I\) is a morphism from \(\varphi\) to \(\varphi'\), the diagram
\[(6.2.1.2) \qquad \xymatrix@C=3em@R=2.5em{ \mathfrak{F}^{I^*}|U \ar[rr]^{t_\sigma} \ar[dr]_{\tau_\varphi} & & \mathfrak{F}^{I'^*}|U \ar[dl]^{\tau_{\varphi'}} \\ & f_! f^* \mathfrak{F}|U & }\]

is commutative. Moreover, \(t_{(\sigma\rho)} = t_\rho t_\sigma\). The \(\psi_f(U)\) form a fibred category \(\psi_f\) over \(S_{\mathrm{ét}}\); the preceding constructions commute with localization and hence define an \(S_{\mathrm{ét}}\)-functor \(\varphi = (V_i)_{i \in I} \in \psi_f(U) \longmapsto \mathfrak{F}^{I^*}|U\) from \(\psi\) to the \(S_{\mathrm{ét}}\)-category of sheaves on étale open subsets of \(S\), and a functor morphism \(\tau_\varphi : \mathfrak{F}^{I^*}|U \longrightarrow f_! f^*\mathfrak{F}|U\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.2.2

(i) The category \(\psi_f\) is locally filtered on the right (IV 14 ) over \(S_{\mathrm{ét}}\).

(ii) The arrows (6.2.1.1) define an isomorphism

\[\tau : \varinjlim_{\varphi = (V_i)_{i \in I} \in \psi_f(U)} \mathfrak{F}^{I^*}|U \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} f_! f^*\mathfrak{F} \, .\]

If \(S\) is strictly local with closed point \(s\), the \(S\)-scheme \(X\) admits a decomposition \(\varphi \in \psi_f(S)\) into open and closed subsets \(X = \coprod_{i \in I} X_i\) indexed by a pointed set \(I\) such that the fibre of \(X_0\) at \(s\) is empty, the \(X_i\) (\(i \neq 0\)) are finite over \(S\) and the fibre of \(X_i\) (\(i \neq 0\)) at \(s\) is reduced to a single point (EGA IV 18.12.1). Such a decomposition is a final object of \(\psi(S)\). Moreover, by 6.1.4 (iii) (or because it is obvious) the fibre at \(s\) of the arrow \(\tau_\varphi\) (6.2.1.1) is an isomorphism.
In the general case, let \(x\) be a geometric point of \(S\) and \(\psi_x\) the fibre of \(\psi_f\) at \(x\),
\[\psi_x = \varinjlim_{U(x)} \psi_f(U) \, ,\]

for \(U\) an étale neighbourhood of \(x\). Let \(S_x\) be the strict localization of \(S\) at \(x\), \(X_x = X \times_S S_x\) and \(f_x : X_x \longrightarrow S_x\). The sorites of passage to the limit show that the category \(\psi_x\) is equivalent to the category \(\psi_{f_x}(S_x)\), hence filtered on the right. It follows that \(\psi\) is locally filtered on the right. Moreover, the fibre at \(x\) of \(\tau\) is identified with the arrow
\[\tau_x : \varinjlim_{\psi_x} \mathfrak{F}^{I_x}_x \longrightarrow (f_! f^*\mathfrak{F})_x\]
and, by what precedes, this arrow is an isomorphism.

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 6.2.3

One can, in one and only one way, define, for every morphism \(f : X \longrightarrow S\), separated, flat of finite presentation and quasi-finite, and every abelian sheaf \(\mathfrak{F}\) on \(S\), a trace morphism

\[\operatorname{Tr}_f : f_! f^*\mathfrak{F} \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}\]

such that the following conditions are satisfied:

(Var 1) \(\operatorname{Tr}_f\) is functorial in \(\mathfrak{F}\).

(Var 2) \(\operatorname{Tr}_f\) is compatible with every base change, i.e. for every cartesian diagram

\[\xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=2em{ X' \ar[r]^{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^{f} \\ S' \ar[r]_{g} & S }\]

the following diagram of functors is commutative:

\[\xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=3em{ f'_! f'^* g^* \ar@{=}[r] \ar[d]_{\operatorname{Tr}_{f'} * g^*} & f'_! g'^* f^* \ar@{=}[r] & g^* f_! f^* \ar[d]^{g^* * \operatorname{Tr}_f} \\ g^* \ar@{=}[rr] & & g^* }\]

(Var 3) \(\operatorname{Tr}_f\) is compatible with composition, i.e. if \(f\) is the composite \(f = gh\) of two separated, flat, finite-presentation and quasi-finite morphisms, the following diagram is commutative:

\[\xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=2.5em{ f_! f^* \ar@{=}[r] \ar[ddr]_{\operatorname{Tr}_f} & g_! h_! h^* g^* \ar[d]^{g_! * \operatorname{Tr}_h * g^*} \\ & g_! g^* \ar[d]^{\operatorname{Tr}_g} \\ & \operatorname{Id} }\]

(Var 4) (Normalization). If \(f\) is finite of constant rank \(n\), the composite homomorphism

\[\mathfrak{F} \longrightarrow f_* f^*\mathfrak{F} = f_! f^*\mathfrak{F} \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}_f} \mathfrak{F}\]

is multiplication by \(n\).
Let us first note that conditions (Var 2) to (Var 4) imply that

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 6.2.3.1

If \(X = X' \sqcup X''\) then, setting \(f' = f|X'\) and \(f'' = f|X''\), the morphism \(\operatorname{Tr}_f\):

\[f_! f^*\mathfrak{F} = f'_! f'^*\mathfrak{F} \oplus f''_! f''^*\mathfrak{F} \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}\]

is the sum of \(\operatorname{Tr}_{f'}\) and \(\operatorname{Tr}_{f''}\).
\[\xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=1.6em{ X' \ar[dr]^{j'} & & \\ & X \ar[r]^{f} & S \\ X'' \ar[ur]_{j''} & & }\]
If we apply (Var 2) to \(j'\), for the base change by \(j'\), and (Var 4) for the identity map, we see that
\[\operatorname{Tr}_{j'} : j'_! j'^* f^*\mathfrak{F} \longrightarrow f^*\mathfrak{F}\]
is the canonical map defined by the decomposition of \(f^*\mathfrak{F}\) into a direct sum
\[f^*\mathfrak{F} = j'_! j'^* f^*\mathfrak{F} \oplus j''_! j''^* f^*\mathfrak{F} \, .\]
If we apply (Var 3) to \(f' = f \circ j'\), we see that the following diagram is commutative
\[\xymatrix@C=3em@R=2.5em{ f'_! f'^*\mathfrak{F} \ar[rr] \ar[dr]_{\operatorname{Tr}_{f'}} & & f_! f^*\mathfrak{F} \ar[dl]^{\operatorname{Tr}_f} \\ & \mathfrak{F} & } \, ,\]
which, together with the analogous statement for \(f''\), is nothing other than 6.2.3.1.

Let \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) be a quasi-finite separated flat morphism of finite presentation. For every \(U \in \operatorname{Ob} S_{\mathrm{ét}}\), let \(\psi'_f(U)\) be the full subcategory of \(\psi_f(U)\) (6.2.1) consisting of the decompositions \((V_i)_{i \in I}\) such that, for \(i \neq 0\), \(V_i\) is locally free of constant rank over \(U\). The categories \(\psi'_f(U)\) form a fibred subcategory of \(\psi_f\), cofinal in \(\psi_f\).

Let \(\mathfrak{F}\) and \(\mathfrak{G}\) be abelian sheaves on \(S\). By 6.2.2 (ii), giving a morphism \(g : f_! f^*\mathfrak{F} \longrightarrow \mathfrak{G}\) amounts to the same thing as giving, for each decomposition \(\varphi = (V_i)_{i \in I} \in \psi'_f(U)\), a morphism \(g_\varphi : \mathfrak{F}^{I^*}|U \longrightarrow \mathfrak{G}|U\), compatible with the morphisms \(t_\sigma\) of (6.2.1.2). If \(f_i\) is the projection of \(V_i\) onto \(U\), \(g_\varphi\) is the arrow whose coordinates are the composite arrows:
\[g_\varphi^i : \mathfrak{F}|U \longrightarrow f_{i*} f_i^* \mathfrak{F}|U \longrightarrow f_! f^*\mathfrak{F}|U \xrightarrow{\;g\;} \mathfrak{G}|U\]

We deduce from this that there exists one and only one arrow \(\operatorname{Tr}_f\), compatible with étale localization and satisfying (Var 4) and 6.2.3.1. It is clear that this arrow satisfies (Var 1) and (Var 2).
To verify (Var 3), we reduce by base change to the easy case where \(S\) is the spectrum of an algebraically closed field.

6.2.4. A weighting of a quasi-finite separated morphism \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) is the datum, for each geometric point \(x\) of \(X\), of an integer \(n(x)\), depending only on the point of \(X\) that is the image of \(x\), this datum satisfying:

(*) For all \(U \in \operatorname{Ob} S_{\mathrm{ét}}\) and every open and closed subset \(X_1\) of \(f^{-1}(U)\), finite over \(U\), the function that associates to each geometric point \(s\) of \(U\) the number \(\sum_{x \in X_1(s)} n(x)\) is locally constant.
If \(f = g h\) is the composite of two weighted morphisms, we weight \(f\) by setting \(n_f(x) = n_h(x) \cdot n_g(h(x))\).
If the morphism \(f'\) is obtained by a base change \(g\) from a weighted morphism \(f\), we weight \(f'\) by setting \(n_{f'}(x) = n_f(g'(x))\).
The preceding arguments in fact prove:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.2.5

One can, in one and only one way, define, for every weighted quasi-finite separated morphism \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) and every abelian sheaf \(\mathfrak{F}\) on \(S\), a trace morphism \(\operatorname{Tr}_f : f_! f^*\mathfrak{F} \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}\), which is functorial in \(\mathfrak{F}\), compatible with base changes and with composition, and satisfies:

(Var'4) If \(f\) is finite and if there exists an integer \(n\) such that, for every geometric point \(s\) of \(S\), we have \(\sum_{x \in X(s)} n(x) = n\), then the composite arrow

\[\mathfrak{F} \longrightarrow f_* f^*\mathfrak{F} = f_! f^*\mathfrak{F} \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}_f} \mathfrak{F}\]

is multiplication by \(n\).

blocks.title: Example
blocks.html:
Example 6.2.6

Let \(S\) be a geometrically unibranch noetherian scheme (for example normal), and \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) a quasi-finite separated morphism. For every geometric point \(x\) of \(X\) with image \(s\) in \(S\), let \(\mathcal{O}_x\) (resp. \(\mathcal{O}_s\)) be the strictly local ring of \(X\) at \(x\) (resp. of \(S\) at \(s\)). The scheme \(\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal{O}_s)\) is reduced and has a unique maximal point \(\eta\). Moreover, \(\mathcal{O}_x\) is finite over \(\mathcal{O}_s\). We set \(n(x) = \operatorname{rg}_\eta(\mathcal{O}_x)\). One verifies that \(n(x)\) is a weighting of \(f\), whence a trace morphism \(\operatorname{Tr}_f\).

6.2.7. Let \(u : X \longrightarrow Y\) be a separated quasi-finite flat morphism of finite presentation. Since the trace morphism (6.2.3) is functorial, it defines, for every complex of abelian sheaves \(K\) on \(Y\), a morphism of complexes
\[(6.2.7.1) \qquad \operatorname{Tr}_u : u_! u^* K \longrightarrow K \, .\]
We shall also call, as we please, trace morphism, Gysin morphism or morphism \(u_*\) any morphism deduced from (6.2.7.1) or 6.2.3 by application of a functor. For example the following ones:
Consider a commutative diagram
\[\xymatrix@C=2em@R=2em{ X \ar[rr]^{u} \ar[dr]_{f} & & Y \ar[dl]^{g} \\ & S & }\]
with \(g\) separated locally of finite type. For every abelian sheaf \(\mathfrak{F}\) on \(Y\), the trace morphism defines a morphism
\[(6.2.7.2) \qquad \operatorname{Tr}_u \text{ ou } u_* : f_! u^* \mathfrak{F} \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} g_! u_! u^* \mathfrak{F} \xrightarrow{g_!(\operatorname{Tr}_u)} g_! \mathfrak{F} \, .\]

If \(g\) is compactifiable, and if \(K\) is a bounded-below complex with torsion cohomology, or a complex of \(g^*\mathcal{A}\)-modules for \(\mathcal{A}\) a sheaf of torsion rings on \(S\), the trace morphism (6.2.7.1) likewise induces

\[(6.2.7.3) \qquad \operatorname{Tr}_u \text{ ou } u_* : Rf_! u^*K \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} Rg_! u_! u^*K \xrightarrow{Rg_!(\operatorname{Tr}_u)} Rg_! K \, ,\] \[(6.2.7.4) \qquad \operatorname{Tr}_u \text{ ou } u_* : R^q f_! u^*K \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} R^q g_! u_! u^*K \xrightarrow{R^q g_!(\operatorname{Tr}_u)} R^q g_! K \, .\]
For \(S\) the spectrum of an algebraically closed field, (6.2.7.4) is a morphism
\[(6.2.7.5) \qquad u_* : H_c^q(X, u^*K) \longrightarrow H_c^q(Y, K)\]
We thus see that cohomology with proper supports presents a covariant character with respect to quasi-finite morphisms.

6.2.8. Let \(u : X \longrightarrow Y\) be as in 6.2.7, \(\Delta_n = [0,n]\) the standard set with \(n + 1\) elements and \(X_n\) the iterated \((n + 1)\)-fold fibre product of \(X\) over \(Y\). The \(X_n\) form a simplicial scheme augmented towards \(Y\) (cf. VI\(_B\)). We shall denote by \(u_n : X_n \longrightarrow Y\) the augmentation morphism. If \(\mathfrak{F}\) is an abelian sheaf on \(Y\), the sheaves \(\mathfrak{F}_n = u_{n!} u_n^*\mathfrak{F}\) form, by virtue of (6.2.7.2) (applied after the change of language \(S \longrightarrow Y\), \(X \longrightarrow X_n\), \(Y \longrightarrow Y\) or \(X_m\)), a simplicial sheaf augmented towards \(\mathfrak{F}\). The differential sheaf of "non-degenerate chains" of this simplicial sheaf has by definition as its \(n^{\text{th}}\) component the quotient of \(\mathfrak{F}_n\), the cokernel of the direct sum of the degeneracy operators with target \(\mathfrak{F}_n\) and of the morphisms \(\sigma \sim \varepsilon(\sigma)\) for \(\sigma\) a symmetry operator.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.2.9

Under the preceding hypotheses, for \(u\) étale separated of finite type surjective and for every abelian sheaf \(\mathfrak{F}\) on \(Y\), we have

(i) The sheaves \(\mathfrak{F}_n\) form a resolution (left) of \(\mathfrak{F}\).

(ii) The differential complex of non-degenerate chains of the simplicial sheaf \((\mathfrak{F}_n)\) is a resolution (left) of \(\mathfrak{F}\). If the geometric fibres of \(u\) all have at most \(d\) points, this resolution is of length \(\leq d\).
By base change, it suffices to verify this statement for \(Y\) the spectrum of an algebraically closed field, in which case 6.2.8 reduces to the computation of the simplicial homology of a simplex.

Let \((U_i)_{i \in I}\) be a finite open covering of the scheme \(Y\), \(\mathfrak{F}\) an abelian sheaf on \(Y\) and, for each subset \(P\) of \(I\), let \(j_P\) be the inclusion of \(U_P = \bigcap_{i \in P} U_i\) into \(X\). Suppose a total order on \(I\) has been chosen. If \(X = \coprod_{i \in I} U_i\) and if \(u\) is the projection of \(X\) onto \(Y\), the resolution 6.2.9 (ii) of \(\mathfrak{F}\) is given by
\[(6.2.9.1) \qquad (\mathfrak{F}_n)_{n\ \mathrm{dég}} = \bigoplus_{|P|=n+1} j_{P!} j_P^* \mathfrak{F} \, .\]
This resolution retains a meaning for \(I\) infinite.

6.2.10. Under the hypotheses of 6.2.9, let \(\mathcal{A}\) be a sheaf of torsion rings on \(Y\) and \(K \in \operatorname{Ob} D^-(Y, \mathcal{A})\). We ring \(X\) by \(u^*\mathcal{A}\). The resolution 6.2.9 (i) (resp. 6.2.9 (ii)), being functorial in \(\mathfrak{F}\), defines a resolution of \(K\) by a double complex \(K_1\). This resolution is called the extraordinary Čech resolution (resp. extraordinary alternating) of \(K\).
Consider a commutative diagram
\[\xymatrix@C=2em@R=2em{ X \ar[rr]^{u} \ar[dr]_{f} & & Y \ar[dl]^{g} \\ & S & }\]

with \(g\) compactifiable. With the notation of 6.2.8, if \(f_n\) is the projection of \(X_n\) onto \(S\), we have \(Rf_{n!} = Rg_! u_{n!}\). The complex \(K_1\), filtered by the semi-simplicial degree, therefore defines a spectral sequence
\[(6.2.10.1) \qquad E_1^{-p,q} = R^q f_{p!} (u_p^* K) \Longrightarrow R^{-p+q} g_! K \, .\]
The differentials \(d_1\) come from the simplicial arrows, so that
\[(6.2.10.2) \qquad E_2^{-p,q} = \mathscr{H}^p (R^q f_{p!} (u_p^* K)) \Longrightarrow R^{-p+q} g_! K \, .\]
Under the hypotheses of (6.2.9.1), we likewise find a spectral sequence
\[(6.2.10.3) \qquad E_1^{-p,q} = \bigoplus_{|P|=p+1} R^q f_{P!} (j_P^* K) \Longrightarrow R^{-p+q} g_! K \, .\]
The spectral sequences (6.2.10.1) and (6.2.10.3) are called the upper localization spectral sequences.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.2.11

If \(f\) is an étale morphism, separated of finite type, the functor \(f_!\) is a left adjoint of the functor \(f^*\), and admits the trace morphism as adjunction arrow.

It is known that if \(X\) is an object of a site \(S\), the functor \(f^*\) of restriction of abelian sheaves to \(X\) admits a left adjoint \(f_!\). If \(F\) is an abelian sheaf on \(X\), \(f_! F\) is the sheaf generated by the presheaf
\[V \longrightarrow \bigoplus_{\xi \in \operatorname{Hom}(V,X)} F(\xi) \, .\]

In the étale case, let us provisionally denote this functor \(f^0_!\). From its adjunction property it follows immediately that its formation commutes with every base change. The trace morphism defines a morphism \(t\) from \(f_! \mathfrak{F}\) to \(f^0_! \mathfrak{F}\), compatible with every base change. It suffices to see that \(t\) is an isomorphism fibre by fibre, i.e. for \(S\) the spectrum of a separably closed field, where this is trivial.
6.2.11.1. One should take care that this interpretation of \(f^0_!\) is specific to the case of the étale site and does not extend to the fpqf site of a prescheme, for example.
6.3. Variant of the trace for continuous coefficients.
In this n° we prove the assertions of GROTHENDIECK [1, n°6], and we apply these results to the definition of a "trace morphism" for suitable fppf sheaves.

6.3.1. Let \(A\) be a commutative ring. If \(L\) and \(M\) are two projective \(A\)-modules of finite type, the map \(u \longmapsto \wedge^m u\), from \(\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\) to \(\operatorname{Hom}(\wedge^m L, \wedge^m M)\), is compatible with every base change and \(m\)-ic (5.5.2). By 5.5.2, it defines a morphism
\[(6.3.1.1) \qquad \wedge^m : \Gamma^m \operatorname{Hom}(L,M) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(\wedge^m L, \wedge^m M)\]

such that, after every base change, for \(u \in \operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\), we have \(\wedge^m(\gamma^m(u)) = \wedge^m u\). Since \(\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\) is flat, this morphism is identified (5.5.2) with a morphism
\[(6.3.1.2) \qquad \wedge^m : \mathrm{TS}^m \operatorname{Hom}(L,M) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(\wedge^m L, \wedge^m M) \, .\]

N.B. One can also define such a homomorphism as soon as 2 is invertible in \(A\): a symmetric element of \(\otimes^m \operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\) defines a symmetric homomorphism from \(\otimes^m L\) to \(\otimes^m M\), and this passes to the quotient to define a homomorphism from \(\wedge^m L\) to \(\wedge^m M\).
Given three projective \(A\)-modules of finite type, the diagram

\[(6.3.1.3) \qquad \xymatrix@C=2em@R=3em{ \Gamma^m \operatorname{Hom}(L,M) \otimes \Gamma^m \operatorname{Hom}(M,N) \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\wedge^m \otimes \wedge^m} & \Gamma^m \operatorname{Hom}(L,N) \ar[d]^{\wedge^m} \\ \operatorname{Hom}(\wedge^m L, \wedge^m M) \otimes \operatorname{Hom}(\wedge^m M, \wedge^m N) \ar[r] & \operatorname{Hom}(\wedge^m L, \wedge^m N) } \, ,\]

in which the horizontal arrows are deduced from the composition arrows (and, for the first, from (5.5.2.8)), is commutative. This translates the formula \(\wedge^m(vu) = \wedge^m v \circ \wedge^m u\).
If \(L\) is a free \(A\)-module of rank \(n\), (6.3.1.2) defines a canonical morphism
\[(6.3.1.4) \qquad \det : \Gamma^n \operatorname{End}_A(L) = \mathrm{TS}^n \operatorname{End}_A(L) \longrightarrow A \, ,\]
which is an algebra homomorphism by 6.3.1.3. By definition, we have
\[(6.3.1.5) \qquad \det(u^{\otimes n}) = \det(u ; L) \, .\]
If \(L\) is moreover a module over an \(A\)-algebra \(B\), (6.3.1.4) defines by composition an algebra homomorphism
\[(6.3.1.6) \qquad \det_L : \mathrm{TS}^n_A(B) \longrightarrow A \, .\]

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 6.3.2

Suppose that \(L\) fits into an exact sequence

\[F : 0 \longrightarrow L' \longrightarrow L \longrightarrow L'' \longrightarrow 0\]

with \(L'\) (resp. \(L''\)) locally free of rank \(n_1\) (resp. \(n_2\)). Let \(n = n_1 + n_2\), \(\alpha\) the "associated graded" morphism from the group \(\operatorname{End}(E)\) of endomorphisms of the extension \(E\) to \(\operatorname{End}(L') \oplus \operatorname{End}(L'')\) and, for \(X\) and \(Y\) two \(A\)-flat modules, let \(\beta\) be the morphism from \(\mathrm{TS}^n(X \oplus Y)\) to \(\mathrm{TS}^{n_1}(X) \otimes \mathrm{TS}^{n_2}(Y)\) deduced from the isomorphism (5.5.2.6)

\[\mathrm{TS}^n(X \oplus Y) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \sum_{n'+n''=n} \mathrm{TS}^{n'}(X) \otimes \mathrm{TS}^{n''}(Y) \, .\]

The following diagram is commutative:

\[\xymatrix@C=1.6em@R=3em{ \mathrm{TS}^n(\operatorname{End}(E)) \ar[r]^-{\mathrm{TS}^n(\alpha)} \ar[d] & \mathrm{TS}^n(\operatorname{End}(L') \oplus \operatorname{End}(L'')) \ar[r]^-{\beta} & \mathrm{TS}^{n_1}(\operatorname{End}(L')) \otimes \mathrm{TS}^{n_2}(\operatorname{End}(L'')) \ar[d]^{\det \otimes \det} \\ \mathrm{TS}^n(\operatorname{End}(L)) \ar[rr]_-{\det} & & A }\]

By the universal property 5.5.2 of \(\mathrm{TS}^n\), it suffices to verify that for \(u \in \operatorname{End}(E)\) the two images of \(u^{\otimes n}\) coincide. If \(\alpha(u) = (u', u'')\), these images are respectively \(\det(u)\) and \(\det(u').\det(u'')\), whence the conclusion.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 6.3.3

Let \(A\) be a ring, \(B\) an \(A\)-algebra, \(C\) a \(B\)-algebra not necessarily commutative, \(E\) a \(B\)-module free of rank \(n\) over \(B\), and \(F\) a \(C\)-module free of rank \(m\) over \(C\). Suppose \(C\) flat over \(A\). By the universal property 5.5.2.2 of \(\Gamma^{nm}\) and 5.5.2.3, there exists a unique arrow \(\sigma : \mathrm{TS}^{nm}_A(C) \longrightarrow \mathrm{TS}^n_A \mathrm{TS}^m_B(C)\) such that after every change of rings \(A \longrightarrow A'\), we have \(\sigma(c^{\otimes nm}) = (c^{\otimes m})^{\otimes n}\). The following diagram is then commutative:

\[\xymatrix@C=3em@R=3em{ \mathrm{TS}^n_A(B) \ar[d]_{\det_E} & \mathrm{TS}^n_A \mathrm{TS}^m_B(C) \ar[l]_-{\mathrm{TS}^n_A(\det_F)} \\ A & \mathrm{TS}^{nm}_A(C) \ar[l]^-{\det_{E \otimes_B F}} \ar[u]_{\sigma} }\]

Proof. By 5.5.2.2 and 5.5.2.3, it suffices to show that the two images of an element \(u^{\otimes nm}\) of \(\mathrm{TS}^{nm}_A(C)\) coincide. These images are \(\det_E(\det_F(u))\) and \(\det_{E \otimes_B F}(u)\); they are expressed in terms of \(A\), \(B\), \(E\), \(F\) and \(u \in \operatorname{End}_B(F)\) and, to verify that they coincide, we may first replace \(B\) by its (commutative) image \(B_1\) in \(\operatorname{End}(E)\), and \(F\) by \(F \otimes_B B_1\). The formula to be proved is then the block-computation formula for determinants (BOURBAKI, Alg. Ch. 8 § 12 lemma 2 p.140).
When \(C\) is no longer necessarily flat over \(A\), the same proof provides more generally a commutative diagram of algebras

\[(6.3.3.1) \qquad \xymatrix@C=3em@R=3em{ \Gamma^n_A(B) \ar[d]_{\det_E} & \Gamma^n_A \Gamma^m_B(C) \ar[l]_-{\Gamma^n_A(\det_F)} \\ A & \Gamma^{nm}_A(C) \ar[l]^-{\det_{E \otimes_B F}} \ar[u]_{\sigma} } \, .\]

6.3.4. If \(B\) is a commutative \(A\)-algebra, \(\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{TS}^n(B))\) is nothing other than the \(n^{\text{th}}\) symmetric power of \(\operatorname{Spec}(B)\) over \(\operatorname{Spec}(A)\), i.e. the quotient of \((\operatorname{Spec}(B)/\operatorname{Spec}(A))^n\) by the symmetric group (SGA 1 IV 3).

If \(X\) is a separated \(S\)-scheme, we shall say that a quasi-coherent \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-module \(\mathfrak{F}\) on \(X\) is finite locally free (resp. and of rank \(n\)) over \(S\) if its support is finite over \(S\) and if its direct image is locally free of finite rank (resp. of rank \(n\)) over \(S\). By support of \(\mathfrak{F}\), we shall again mean the subscheme of \(X\) defined by the vanishing of \(\mathfrak{F}\) (which is a quasi-coherent Ideal, \(\mathfrak{F}\) being quasi-coherent of finite type).

If \(\mathfrak{F}\) is finite locally free over \(S\), of rank \(n\) and with support \(E\), the scheme \(E\) is affine over \(S\); by globalization over \(S\), \(\mathfrak{F}\) defines, via (6.3.1.6), a section \(\sigma_E(\mathfrak{F})\) of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(E)\), whence, by functoriality, a section \(\sigma(\mathfrak{F})\) of the algebraic space(∗) \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)\),
\[(6.3.4.1) \qquad \sigma(\mathfrak{F}) \in \Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)/S) \, .\]
In particular, if \(f : S' \longrightarrow S\) is finite locally free of rank \(n\), we obtain, for \(\mathfrak{F} = \mathcal{O}_{S'}\), a canonical section
\[(6.3.4.2) \qquad t \in \Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(S')/S) \, .\]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.5

Let \(X\) be a separated scheme over \(S\) and \(\mathfrak{F}_1\), \(\mathfrak{F}_2\) two \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules finite locally free of rank \(n_1\) and \(n_2\) over \(S\). Set \(n = n_1 + n_2\). Let \(d\) be the canonical arrow \(d : \operatorname{Sym}^{n_1}_S(X) \times \operatorname{Sym}^{n_2}_S(X) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)\). If \(\mathfrak{F}\) is an extension of \(\mathfrak{F}_1\) by \(\mathfrak{F}_2\), we have

\[\sigma(\mathfrak{F}) = d(\sigma(\mathfrak{F}_1), \sigma(\mathfrak{F}_2)) \, .\]
We may replace \(X\) by the support (finite over \(S\)) of \(\mathfrak{F}_1 \oplus \mathfrak{F}_2\) and assume \(S\) affine. Translated in terms of rings, the proposition then follows from 6.3.2.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 6.3.6

If \(X\) is a separated scheme over \(S\), \(\mathfrak{F}\) a \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-module finite locally free of rank \(n\) over \(S\) and if \(\mathcal{L}\) is an invertible sheaf on \(X\), we have

\[\sigma(\mathfrak{F}) = \sigma(\mathfrak{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}) \, .\]
Let us replace \(X\) by the support (6.3.4) of \(\mathfrak{F}\); locally on \(S\), \(\mathcal{L}\) is then isomorphic to \(\mathcal{O}_X\), and the assertion becomes trivial.
The reader will verify:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.7

For every diagram of \(S\)-schemes separated over \(S\)

\[\xymatrix@C=2em@R=2em{ X \ar[rr]^{u} \ar[dr]_{f} & & Y \ar[dl]^{g} \\ & S & }\]

and every \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-module \(\mathfrak{F}\) finite locally free of rank \(n\) over \(S\), the \(\mathcal{O}_Y\)-module \(u_* \mathfrak{F}\) is finite locally free of rank \(n\) over \(S\), and

\[u(\sigma(\mathfrak{F})) = \sigma(u_* \mathfrak{F}) \, .\]
6.3.7.1. Let us finally note that the construction of the morphisms \(\sigma\) (6.3.4.1) and \(t\) (6.3.4.2) is compatible with every base change, which makes sense by 5.5.2.7.
Application 1. The case of smooth curves.

6.3.8. Let \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) be a smooth quasi-projective curve over \(S\), i.e. a smooth quasi-projective morphism purely of relative dimension 1. The theory of Hilbert schemes [GROTHENDIECK [1]] shows that the fpqc sheaf \(\underline{\mathrm{Div}}^n_{X/S}\) which, to each \(S\)-scheme \(S'\), associates the set of relative divisors on \(X' = X \times_S S'\) that are finite over \(S\) and of degree \(n\), is a representable sheaf.

For each relative divisor \(E\) on \(X\), finite of degree \(n\) over \(S\), we have a canonical element (6.3.4.2) \(t(E) \in \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(E)\), with image \(\sigma(E)\) in \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)\). This construction, being compatible with every base change, defines
\[(6.3.8.1) \qquad \sigma : \underline{\mathrm{Div}}^n_{X/S} \longrightarrow \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X) : E \longrightarrow \sigma(\mathcal{O}_E) \, .\]
Each section \(s\) of \(f\) defines a relative divisor finite over \(S\) of degree 1, the divisor \(s(S)\). The morphism
\[(X/S)^n \longrightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Div}}^n_{X/S} : (s_i)_{0 < i \leq n} \longmapsto \sum s_i(S)\]
is symmetric, and hence induces a morphism
\[(6.3.8.2) \qquad \alpha : \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X) \longrightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Div}}^n_{X/S} \, .\]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.9

The morphisms \(\sigma\) and \(\alpha\) of 6.3.8 are mutually inverse isomorphisms.
Proof. a) \(\sigma \alpha = \operatorname{Id}\). It suffices to prove that the composite arrow
\[(X/S)^n \xrightarrow{\;\pi\;} \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X) \xrightarrow{\;\alpha\;} \underline{\mathrm{Div}}^n_{X/S} \xrightarrow{\;\sigma\;} \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X)\]
is \(\pi\). For \(n = 1\), the assertion is clear; the general case follows from it via the

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 6.3.9.1

With the notation of 6.3.5 and (6.3.8.1), we have

\[\sigma(E + F) = d(\sigma(E), \sigma(F)) \, .\]
This lemma follows from 6.3.5, 6.3.6 and from the exact sequence
\[0 \longrightarrow \mathcal{O}(-F) \otimes \mathcal{O}_E \longrightarrow \mathcal{O}_{E+F} \longrightarrow \mathcal{O}_F \longrightarrow 0 \, .\]

b) It is known that \(\underline{\mathrm{Div}}^n_{X/S}\) is smooth over \(S\) (there is no obstruction to lifting divisors on a curve infinitesimally (cf. SGA 3 XI 1)). The morphism \(\alpha \pi : (X/S)^n \longrightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Div}}^n_{X/S}\) is a quasi-finite surjective morphism between schemes smooth over \(S\) whose source has equidimensional fibres. It is therefore flat (EGA \(\mathrm{O}_{IV}\) 17.3.5), hence \(\alpha \pi\) is an epimorphism of fppf sheaves, hence so is \(\alpha\). Taking a) into account, this completes the proof of 6.3.9.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 6.3.10

Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, \(M\) a free \(k\)-module and \(u\) an endomorphism of \(M\). Denote by \(N_{\det(u-T)=0}\) the norm from \(k[T]/\det(u-T)\) to \(k\). For \(P \in k[T]\), we then have

\[N_{\det(u-T)=0}(P(T)) = \det(P(u), M) \, .\]

It is a matter of verifying an algebraic identity between the coefficients of the matrix of \(u\) and the coefficients of \(P\). To prove 6.3.10, it therefore suffices (thanks to familiar arguments) to treat the case where \(k\) is an algebraically closed field and \(u\) is semi-simple, with eigenvalues \(a_i\).
We then have
\[\det(u - T) = \prod (a_i - T)\] \[N_{\det(u - T) = 0}(P(T)) = \prod P(a_i) \qquad \text{and}\] \[\det(P(u), M) = \prod P(a_i) \, .\]

6.3.11.0. Let \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) be a quasi-projective morphism, of finite presentation, flat with fibres purely of dimension 1 and Cohen-Macaulay; these conditions are thus satisfied if \(X\) is a smooth quasi-projective curve over \(S\). Let \(\mathfrak{F}\) be an \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-module, finite locally free over \(S\). Since the module \(\mathfrak{F}\) is zero on a fibrewise dense open subset of \(X\), we have a canonical arrow \(\psi : \mathcal{O}_X \longrightarrow \det{}^*(\mathfrak{F})\) (SGA 6 XI or MUMFORD [1 Ch. 5 § 3]). We shall denote by \(\delta(\mathfrak{F})\) the divisor defined by the annihilator ideal of \(\operatorname{coker}(\psi)\) (Ibidem); this divisor is finite over \(S\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.11.1

Under the hypotheses 6.3.11.0 and with the notation of 6.3.8 and (6.3.4.1), if \(\mathfrak{F}\) is of rank \(n\), then \(\delta(\mathfrak{F})\) is of degree \(n\) and

\[\sigma(\mathfrak{F}) = \sigma(\delta(\mathfrak{F})) \, .\]

Proof. a) Case \(f\) smooth. We reduce in the standard way to the case \(S\) local artinian with algebraically closed residue field. The additivity (6.3.5) of \(\sigma\) allows us to assume the support of \(\mathfrak{F}\) concentrated at a rational point \(x\) of \(X\). One verifies immediately that if \(T\) is a uniformizer at \(x\), defining \(p : X \longrightarrow \mathbb{E}^1_S\), then \(p_*(\mathcal{O}_{\delta(\mathfrak{F})}) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \mathcal{O}_{\delta(p_*\mathfrak{F})}\) (since the constructions carried out commute with passage to the completion). By this and 6.3.7 we reduce to the case where \(X = \mathbb{E}^1_S\).

If \(X = \mathbb{E}^1_S\) and if \(S\) is affine, \(S = \operatorname{Spec}(k)\), then \(\mathfrak{F}\) is identified with a locally free \(k\)-module \(M\), equipped with an endomorphism \(u\) (the action of \(T\)). The module \(M\), as a \(k[T]\)-module, admits the resolution
\[0 \longrightarrow k[T] \otimes_k M \xrightarrow{\;\varphi\;} k[T] \otimes_k M \xrightarrow{\;\varepsilon\;} M \longrightarrow 0 \, ,\]

where \(\varepsilon(P \otimes m) = P(u)(m)\) and where \(\varphi(1 \otimes m) = 1 \otimes um - T \otimes m\). From the formula \(\varphi = u - T\), we deduce that the divisor \(\delta(\mathfrak{F})\) has equation \(\det(u - T, M) = 0\).
To verify 6.3.11, it suffices to show that, after every base change and for every \(\varphi\) a section of \(\mathcal{O}_X\), we have
\[\det_k(\varphi, M) = \det_k(\varphi, \mathcal{O}_{\delta(\mathfrak{F})}) \quad (= N_{\delta(\mathfrak{F})/S}(\varphi)) \, .\]
For \(f = P(T)\), this is what 6.3.10 asserts.
b) General case. Let us first make explicit the statement to be proved in the following more concrete form:

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 6.3.11.2

Under the hypotheses 6.3.11.0 on \(f : X \longrightarrow S\), let \(M\) be a locally free module of finite type on \(X\), and \(u\) an endomorphism of \(M\) such that \(\det u\) is a section of \(\underline{\mathcal{O}}_X\) regular on each fibre \(X_s\) (from which it follows that \(\operatorname{Coker} u = M/u(M)\) and \(\operatorname{Coker} \det u = \underline{\mathcal{O}}_X/\det u\) are both flat of finite presentation over \(S\) and with quasi-finite fibres). Suppose that the common support of these sheaves is finite over \(S\), so that they define locally free sheaves of finite type over \(S\). Then for every section \(\varphi\) of \(\underline{\mathcal{O}}_X\), the determinants with respect to \(\underline{\mathcal{O}}_S\) of \(\varphi\) acting on \(\operatorname{Coker} u\) and on \(\operatorname{Coker} \det u\) are equal:

\[(6.3.11.3) \qquad \det_S(\varphi, M/u(M)) = \det_S(\varphi, \underline{\mathcal{O}}_X/\det u) \, .\]

Note that this statement implies the equality of the ranks of the two locally free Modules considered over \(S\), for reasons of homogeneity (when one replaces \(\varphi\) by \(T \varphi\), \(T\) an "indeterminate" section of \(\underline{\mathcal{O}}_S\)). Moreover, replacing \(\varphi\) by \(1 + T \varphi\), where \(T\) is such an indeterminate (more precisely, one makes a base change \(S' = S[T] \longrightarrow S\)), one deduces from (6.3.11.3) the apparently more general formula
\[(6.3.11.4) \qquad \operatorname{Pol}_S(\varphi, M/uM)(T) = \operatorname{Pol}_S(\varphi, \underline{\mathcal{O}}_X/\det u)(T)\]
on the characteristic polynomials.

To prove 6.3.11.3, we shall reduce to the smooth case already proved. By étale localization on \(S\), we reduce to the case where \(S\) is strictly local with closed point \(s\), then by additivity we reduce to the case where the support of \(M/u(M)\) has a single point over \(X_s\), say \(x\). Up to making a flat extension of the base, we may assume the residue extension \(k(x)/k(s)\) trivial, and up to replacing \(X\) by a sufficiently small neighbourhood of \(x\), and adding to \(\varphi\) a function that induces the zero operation on \(M/u(M)\) and on \(\underline{\mathcal{O}}_X/\det u\) (which does not modify the formula to be proved), one easily sees that we may assume that \(\varphi\) induces a section of \(\underline{\mathcal{O}}_{X_s}\) regular at \(x\), hence (up to shrinking \(X\)) defines a quasi-finite flat morphism
\[p : X \longrightarrow X' = S[T] \, .\]

By étale localization on \(X\) and on \(X'\), we may therefore assume that we have a finite and flat morphism \(p\) as above, with \(X'\) smooth over \(S\), and \(\varphi = p^*(\varphi')\), where \(\varphi'\) is a section of \(\underline{\mathcal{O}}_{X'}\). Let us then set

\[\begin{aligned} & M' = p_*(M) \, , \quad u' = p_*(u) \, , \\ & P = \operatorname{Coker} u, \quad Q = \operatorname{Coker} \det u \, , \\ & P' = \operatorname{Coker} u', \quad Q' = \operatorname{Coker} \det u' \, . \end{aligned}\]
It is known that we have
\[\det u' = N_{X'/X} \det u, \quad \text{hence} \quad Q' = \operatorname{Coker} N_{X'/X}(\det u) \, .\]
We have trivially
\[\det_S(\varphi, P) = \det_S(\varphi', P') \, ,\]
and by the formula (6.3.11.3) proved in the smooth case,
\[\det_S(\varphi', P') = \det_S(\varphi', Q') \, ,\]
so that it remains to prove the formula
\[\det_S(\varphi', Q') = \det_S(\varphi, Q) \, ,\]

which is equivalent to the formula (6.3.11.3) to be established. We thus see that its validity depends only on the section \(\det u\) of \(\underline{\mathcal{O}}_X\), or again that it is equivalent to the same formula in the case where \(M\) is replaced by \(\underline{\mathcal{O}}_X\), and \(\varphi\) by \(\det u\). But in the case \(M = \underline{\mathcal{O}}_X\) the formula (6.3.11.3) is tautological! This completes the proof.

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.html:
Remark 6.3.11.5

In the case where \(S\) is artinian, the equality of the ranks over \(S\) of \(\operatorname{Coker} u\) and \(\operatorname{Coker} \det u\) (notation of 6.3.11.2) is a special case of EGA IV 21.10.17.3, of which (6.3.11.3) may be regarded as a "relative" version.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.12

Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be two quasi-projective curves of finite presentation, flat with Cohen-Macaulay fibres over \(S\), and \(u : X \longrightarrow Y\) a quasi-finite flat morphism.

The following diagram

\[\xymatrix@C=3em@R=2.5em{ \underline{\mathrm{Div}}^n_{X/S} \ar[r]^{u_*} \ar[d]_{\sigma_X} & \underline{\mathrm{Div}}^n_{Y/S} \ar[d]^{\sigma_Y} \\ \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(X) \ar[r]_{\operatorname{Sym}^n(u)} & \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(Y) }\]

is then commutative(∗).
Since \(u_*(D) = \delta(u_* \mathcal{O}_D)\), 6.3.12 follows from 6.3.7 and 6.3.11.1.
Application 2. The trace morphism.
6.3.13. Let \(G\) be an abelian sheaf on the large fppf site of a scheme \(S\) (0.10). Suppose that \(G\) satisfies the following condition.
(6.3.13.1). For every affine flat morphism of finite presentation \(f : X \longrightarrow Y\) of \(S\)-schemes, and for every integer \(n \geq 1\), the morphism
\[\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Sym}^n_Y(X), G) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_S((X/Y)^n, G)\]
is injective and has as image the set of symmetric morphisms from \((X/Y)^n\) to \(G\).
This condition is stable under base change.

Let \(f : T \longrightarrow S\) be a finite locally free morphism of rank \(n\). Let \(\operatorname{pr}_i\) be the \(i^{\text{th}}\) projection of \((T/S)^n\) into \(T\), and \(t\) the section (6.3.4.2) of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(T)\). If \(u \in G(T)\), then \(\sum \operatorname{pr}_i^*(u)\) is a symmetric element of \(G((T/S)^n)\) and hence defines
\[u_n \in G(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(T)) \, .\]
We set
\[\operatorname{Tr}_f(u) = t^*(u_n) \, .\]

When \(f\) is finite locally free, we define \(\operatorname{Tr}_f(u)\), locally on \(S\), by the preceding formula. This construction is compatible with every base change and hence defines a trace morphism
\[(6.3.13.2) \qquad \operatorname{Tr}_f : f_* f^*G \longrightarrow G \, .\]
6.3.14. The condition (6.3.13.1) is satisfied in the following cases
a) If \(G\) is representable, by definition of the symmetric powers.
b) For \(G\) the inverse image on \(S_{\mathrm{fppf}}\) of a sheaf on the small étale site of \(S\) (0.10).
c) For \(G\) defined by a quasi-coherent \(\mathcal{O}_S\)-module \(G_0\).
Statement c) reduces to (5.5.2.7).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.15

For \(G\) satisfying (6.3.13.1), we have:

(i) The morphism \(\operatorname{Tr}_f\) is functorial in \(G\), hence additive.

(ii) Its formation is compatible with every base change \(S' \longrightarrow S\).

(iii) If \(T = \coprod_i T_i\), so that \(f_* G \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \sum f_{i*} G\), we have \(\operatorname{Tr}_f = \sum \operatorname{Tr}_{f_i}\).

(iv) If \(T\) is of constant rank \(n\) over \(S\), the composite morphism

\[G \longrightarrow f_* f^*G \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}_f} G\]

is multiplication by \(n\).

(v) The trace morphism is compatible with composition (cf. 6.2.3 Var 3).

Assertions (i) and (ii) are clear, and (iii) is an easy consequence of 6.3.5. With the notation of 6.3.13, if \(u \in G(S)\), then \(u_n\) is \(n\) times the inverse image of \(u\), so that \(\operatorname{Tr}_f(f^*u) = t^*(u_n) = n u\).
To prove (v), we reduce, by étale localization on \(S\) and using (iii), to proving that for
\[f = gh : S'' \xrightarrow{\;h\;} S' \xrightarrow{\;g\;} S \, ,\]
with \(f\) and \(g\) finite locally free of constant ranks \(n\) and \(m\), the diagram
\[(6.3.15.1) \qquad \xymatrix@C=3em@R=2.5em{ G(S'') \ar[rr]^{\operatorname{Tr}_h} \ar[dr]_{\operatorname{Tr}_f} & & G(S') \ar[dl]^{\operatorname{Tr}_g} \\ & G(S) & }\]
is commutative. For \(u \in G(S'')\), let us consider the diagram

\[(6.3.15.2) \qquad \xymatrix@C=2.6em@R=3em{ \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(S') \ar[rr]^{\operatorname{Sym}^n(t)} \ar[dr]|-{\operatorname{Tr}_g(u)_n} & & \operatorname{Sym}^n_S \operatorname{Sym}^m_{S'}(S'') \ar[dl]|-{(u_m)_n} \\ & G & \\ S \ar[uu]^{t} \ar[rr]_{t} \ar@/^0.7em/[ur]|-{\operatorname{Tr}_f \operatorname{Tr}_g(u)} \ar@/_0.9em/[ur]|-{\operatorname{Tr}_{fg}(u)} & & \operatorname{Sym}^{nm}_S(S'') \ar[uu]_{\sigma} \ar[ul]|-{u_{nm}} }\]
The right vertical arrow is defined because \(S'\) is flat over \(S\); each triangle is commutative and (v) will therefore be a consequence of the commutativity of the outer boundary.
Translating in terms of rings, this is a consequence of the special case \(B = E\) and \(C = F\) of 6.3.3.

6.3.16. Let now \(f : T \longrightarrow S\) be a quasi-finite flat morphism of finite presentation. If \(\mathfrak{F}\) is an fppf sheaf on \(T\), we define its direct image with proper support \(f_! \mathfrak{F}\) on \(S\) as the presheaf which to \(S'/S\) associates the set of sections of \(F\) on \(T'\) whose support is proper over \(S'\). This presheaf is a sheaf by 6.1.1. With the notation of 6.1.1, we can also express it as a local inductive limit (IV 14. ).
\[f_! F = \varinjlim_{V \in \varphi(U)} f_*(F|V) \, ,\]
a formula which accounts for the fairly obvious fact that the properties of \(f_!\) reduce to those of \(f'_*\) for \(f'\) finite. We thus find:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.17

One can, in one and only one way, define, for every morphism \(f : T \longrightarrow S\) quasi-finite flat of finite presentation and for every fppf sheaf \(G\) on \(S\) satisfying (6.3.13.1), a trace morphism

\[\operatorname{Tr}_f : f_! f^*G \longrightarrow G\]

satisfying:

(i) For \(f\) finite we recover the morphism (6.3.13.2).

(ii) The conditions (Var 1) to (Var 4) of 6.2.3 are fulfilled, mutatis mutandis.
The quasi-finite morphism \(f\) induces a commutative diagram (cf. (0.11)) of sites (in which \(\alpha_*\) is the "restriction" functor):
\[\xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=2.5em{ T_{\mathrm{fppf}} \ar[r]^{\alpha} \ar[d]_{f} & T_{\mathrm{ét}} \ar[d]^{f_{\mathrm{ét}}} \\ S_{\mathrm{fppf}} \ar[r]_{\alpha} & S_{\mathrm{ét}} }\]
We have, for \(G\) on \(T_{\mathrm{fppf}}\),
\[f_! \alpha_* \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \alpha_* f_! \, .\]
We also have a "base-change" morphism
\[c : f_{\mathrm{ét}}^* \alpha_* \longrightarrow \alpha_* f^* \, .\]

We leave to the reader the task of verifying the following compatibility between the trace morphisms 6.2.3 and 6.3.17. For \(G\) on \(S_{\mathrm{fppf}}\) satisfying (6.3.13.1), the following diagram is commutative:

\[(6.3.17.1) \qquad \xymatrix@C=2.6em@R=3em{ f_{\mathrm{ét}!} f_{\mathrm{ét}}^* \alpha_* G \ar[r]^-{f_! \mathrm{ch}} \ar[d]_{\operatorname{Tr}_f} & f_{\mathrm{ét}!} \alpha_* f^*G & \alpha_* f_! f^*G \ar[l]_-{\sim} \ar[d]^{\alpha_* \operatorname{Tr}_f} \\ \alpha_* G \ar@{=}[rr] & & \alpha_* G }\]

In more concrete terms, this means that if \(G\) is an fppf sheaf on \(S\), which by restriction to the étale site defines an étale sheaf \(\alpha_*G\), and if \(u\) is a section with proper support of the inverse image \(f_{\mathrm{ét}}^*(\alpha_*G)\), with image \(u_1\) in \(f^*G\), the elements \(\operatorname{Tr}_f(u)\) (in the sense of 6.2.3) and \(\operatorname{Tr}_f(u_1)\) (in the sense of 6.2.17) coincide in \(G(S)\).

blocks.title: Example
blocks.html:
Example 6.3.18

Let \(f : S' \longrightarrow S\) be a finite locally free morphism of rank \(n\) and \(u \in \Gamma(S', \mathcal{O}_{S'}) = \operatorname{Hom}_S(S', \mathbb{E}^1_S)\). The morphism \(u\) defines a morphism

\[\operatorname{Sym}(u) : \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(S') \longrightarrow \operatorname{Sym}^n_S(\mathbb{E}^1_S) = \operatorname{Spec}(S[\sigma_1 \ldots \sigma_n]) \, ,\]

where the \(\sigma_i\) are elementary symmetric functions (cf. BOURBAKI, Alg. 5, App. I n°2). We then have (by an easy computation left to the reader):

\[(6.3.18.1) \qquad [\operatorname{Sym}(u) \circ t]^*(\sigma_i) = \sigma_i(u) \, ,\]

where \(t \in \Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(S')/S)\) is the canonical element (6.3.4.2), and where \(\sigma_i(u)\) denotes the \(i^{\text{th}}\) coefficient of the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by \(u\) in \(f_* \mathcal{O}_{S'}\). We deduce from this that the "trace" maps

\[\begin{cases} \mathbb{G}_a(S') \longrightarrow \mathbb{G}_a(S) \\[4pt] \mathbb{G}_m(S') \longrightarrow \mathbb{G}_m(S) \end{cases}\]

are respectively the usual trace and norm; indeed, the morphism \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(\mathbb{E}^1_S) \longrightarrow \mathbb{E}^1_S\) deduced from the additive (resp. multiplicative) law on \(\mathbb{E}^1_S\) is given by the function \(\sigma_1\) (resp. \(\sigma_n\)) on \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(\mathbb{E}^1_S) \simeq \operatorname{Spec}(S[\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n])\).

We then deduce from (6.3.17.1) that for \(n\) invertible on \(S\) the diagram of étale sheaves

\[(6.3.18.2) \qquad \xymatrix@C=2em@R=3em{ 0 \ar[r] & f_* \mu_n \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\operatorname{Tr}_f} & f_* \mathbb{G}_m \ar[r] \ar[d]^{N_f} & f_* \mathbb{G}_m \ar[r] \ar[d]^{N_f} & 0 \\ 0 \ar[r] & \mu_n \ar[r] & \mathbb{G}_m \ar[r] & \mathbb{G}_m \ar[r] & 0 }\]

is commutative.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.19

Let there be a commutative diagram

\[\xymatrix@C=2em@R=2em{ X \ar[rr]^{u} \ar[dr]_{p} & & Y \ar[dl]^{q} \\ & S & }\]

in which \(X\) and \(Y\) are smooth quasi-projective curves over \(S\) and \(u\) a quasi-finite morphism.

(i) If \(D\) is a divisor on \(X\) finite over \(S\) (see note p.192) and \(g\) a section of \(G_Y\) over \(Y\), we have

\[\operatorname{Tr}_{D/S}(u^*g) = \operatorname{Tr}_{(u_* D)/S}(g) \, .\]

(ii) If \(E\) is a divisor on \(Y\) finite over \(S\), \(g\) a section of \(G_X\) over \(X\) and if \(u\) is finite, we have

\[\operatorname{Tr}_{E/S}(\operatorname{Tr}_{X/Y}(g)) = \operatorname{Tr}_{(u^* E)/S}(g) \, .\]
Proof. (i) Let \(g_n\) be the section of \(G\) over \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_S(Y)\) deduced from \(g\) (6.3.13). By 6.3.12, we have
\[\operatorname{Tr}_{D/S}(u^*g) \underset{\mathrm{dfn}}{=} \sigma(D)^*(u^*g)_n = \sigma(D)^*(u^*g_n) = (u \circ \sigma(D))^*(g_n) = \sigma(u_* D)^*(g_n) = \operatorname{Tr}_{u_* D}(g_n) \, .\]
(ii) Formula (ii) follows from 6.3.15 (ii) and (v):
\[\operatorname{Tr}_{E/S}(\operatorname{Tr}_{X/Y}(g)) = \operatorname{Tr}_{E/S}(\operatorname{Tr}_{u^*E/E}(g)) = \operatorname{Tr}_{u^*E/S}(g) \, .\]
Application 3. Trace of a torsor.

6.3.20. Let \(G\) be a sheaf on the big fppf site of \(S\) satisfying (6.3.13.1). Let \(u : X \longrightarrow Y\) be a finite locally free morphism of \(S\)-schemes and \(K\) a \(G_X\)-torsor on \(X\). Suppose that, locally fppf over \(Y\), the torsor \(K\) on \(X\) is trivial. This is the case if \(K\) is trivial locally for the étale topology.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.21

Under the hypotheses 6.3.20, there exists, up to unique isomorphism, one and only one torsor \(\operatorname{Tr}_u(K)\) under \(G_Y\) on \(Y\), equipped with a morphism \(\operatorname{Tr}_u\) or \(\operatorname{Tr}_u^K : u_*K \longrightarrow \operatorname{Tr}_u(K)\), which, for \(g\) a local section (in the fppf sense) of \(G\) on \(Y\) and \(k\) a local section of \(u_*K\), satisfies

\[\operatorname{Tr}_u^K(g\, k) = \operatorname{Tr}_u(g) \cdot \operatorname{Tr}_u^K(k) \, .\]

The problem is local on \(Y\); we may therefore assume \(K\) trivial: \(K = G_X\). A solution of the problem is to take \(K = G_Y\) and, as trace morphism, the morphism (6.3.13.2). One checks at once that it is the only one.
The trace functor 6.3.20 is defined in particular when \(G\) satisfies the following condition
(6.3.21.1) For every \(S\)-scheme \(X\), every torsor under \(G_X\) on \(X\) is locally trivial for the étale topology.
This condition is satisfied for \(G\) a smooth group, for \(G\) the inverse image of a sheaf on the small étale site of \(S\), or for \(G\) defined by a quasi-coherent sheaf on \(S\).
By construction, we have
\[(6.3.21.2) \qquad \operatorname{Tr}_u(K) = u_*(K) \times_{u_* G_X} G_Y \, .\]

6.3.22. To define a trace functor under more general hypotheses, the key point is, for \(f : X \longrightarrow T\) a flat quasi-projective morphism of finite presentation of \(S\)-schemes, to define a reasonable functor \(K \longmapsto K_n\) from the \(G_X\)-torsors on \(X\) to the \(G_Z\)-torsors on \(Z = \operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\).
First of all, \(f_n\) denoting the projection of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\) onto \(T\), we have the following lemma, which is proved like 6.3.21:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 6.3.22.1

With the preceding notation and if, locally on \(T\), the torsor \(K\) is trivial, then there exists, up to unique isomorphism, one and only one torsor \(K_n\) on \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\), equipped with a morphism \(\alpha : f_*K \longrightarrow f_{n*}(K_n)\), which for \(g\) a local section (fppf) of \(f_* G_X\) and \(k\) a local section of \(u_*K\) satisfies

\[\alpha(g\, k) = g_n \circ \alpha(k)\]

(notation of 6.3.13 for \(g_n\) ; the definition of \(g_n\) here uses the flatness hypothesis etc).
The general case will be treated by a somewhat contrived descent argument. First of all:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.23

Let there be a commutative diagram

\[(6.3.23.1) \qquad \xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=2em{ X \ar[rr]^{u} \ar[dr] & & Y \ar[dl] \\ & T & }\]

of \(T\)-schemes flat of finite presentation and quasi-projective, with \(u\) étale surjective. Then the semi-simplicial system of schemes \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T((X/Y)^{k+1})\) is a hypercovering for the étale topology of the scheme \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Y)\).
Proof. a) We shall need to use the auxiliary result:

6.3.23.2. Let \((X,Y,T)\) be as above, \(t \in T\), \(Z\) a \(T\)-scheme which is the sum of a finite number of \(T\)-schemes \(\operatorname{Spec}(k_i)\), for \(k_i\) a finite extension of \(k_t\), and a commutative diagram of \(T\)-schemes
\[(6.3.23.3) \qquad \xymatrix@C=2em@R=2em{ & Z \ar[dl]_{x} \ar[dr]^{y} & \\ X_t \ar[rr]_{u} & & Y_t } \, ,\]

such that \(x\) and \(y\) are closed immersions. Let \(z \in \operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Z)\), and let \(x(Z)\) and \(y(Z)\) be its images in \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\) and \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Y)\). Then \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(u)\) is étale at \(x(Z)\).

The formation of the scheme \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\) is compatible with every base change \(S' \longrightarrow S\) (5.5.2.7). By reduction to the noetherian case, we deduce that \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\) is of finite presentation over \(S\); moreover it is flat over \(S\) (5.5.2.4). Thanks to the fibrewise flatness criterion, to prove (6.3.23.2) we reduce to the case where \(S\) is the spectrum of a field. The completion of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\) at \(Z\) then has as affine algebra the projective limit of the affine algebras localized at \(x(Z)\) of the schemes \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Z_k)\), for \(Z_k\) an infinitesimal neighbourhood of \(Z\) in \(X\). By hypothesis, \(u\) induces isomorphisms between the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of \(Z\) in \(X\) and in \(Y\). The completion of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(u)\) at \(x(z)\) and \(y(z)\) is therefore an isomorphism, and this proves (6.3.23.2).

We deduce from 6.3.23.2 that the sum scheme, for \(z \in \operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Z)\), of the henselizations at \(y(z)\) of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Y)\) depends only on \(Z\) and on the \(T\)-scheme \(X_Z^h\), the sum of the henselizations of \(X\) at the various points of \(Z\). We shall denote this scheme by the notation \(\operatorname{Sym}^{h,n}_T(X_Z^h)\) ; it is functorial in \(X_Z^h\).

b) By passage to the limit, to prove 6.3.23, it suffices to show that for \(y \in \operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Y)\), closed in its fibre, the inverse image on the henselization of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Y)\) at \(y\) of the simplicial scheme \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T((X/Y)^{k+1})\) is a hypercovering for the étale topology. This problem is local on \(T\) for the étale topology; we thereby reduce to the case where there exists a diagram (6.3.23.3) with \(y = x(Z)\) (by killing the residue extensions by a separable extension of \(k_t\)). The semi-simplicial system under consideration is then deduced from the system
\[\operatorname{Sym}^{h,n}_T((X^h_{u^{-1}(Z)}/Y^h_Z)^{k+1}), \quad \text{augmented to} \quad \operatorname{Sym}^{h,n}_T(Y^h_Z)\]

by base change, so that it suffices to consider the latter. The semi-simplicial system of the \((X^h_{u^{-1}(Z)}/Y^h_Z)^{k+1}\) is semi-simplicially homotopic to the constant system \(Y^h_Z\), since \(X^h_{u^{-1}(Z)}/Y^h_Z\) admits a section. The system \(\operatorname{Sym}^{h,n}_T((X^h_{u^{-1}(Z)}/Y^h_Z)^{h+1})\) is therefore likewise homotopic to \(\operatorname{Sym}^{h,n}_T(Y^h_Z)\), and in particular is a hypercovering of it. This proves 6.3.23.
6.3.24. Let \(f : Y \longrightarrow T\) be a flat quasi-projective morphism of finite presentation of \(S\)-schemes, and \(K\) a \(G_Y\)-torsor on \(Y\). Consider the following problem:

6.3.24.0. To define, for every morphism \(u : X \longrightarrow Y\), with \(X\) quasi-projective flat of finite presentation over \(T\), a torsor \((u^*K)_n\) on \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\), and for every \(v : X' \longrightarrow X\) an isomorphism \(c_v : (v^*u^*K)_n \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \operatorname{Sym}^n_T(v)^*K_n\), such that
(i) the isomorphisms \(c_v\) are compatible with composition;
(ii) for \(u^*K\) locally trivial over \(T\), one recovers the torsor of 6.3.22.1, and its variance.

By 6.3.23, the question of existence and uniqueness of a solution to 6.3.24.0, for every torsor deduced from \(K\) by an inverse image of the type considered in 6.3.24.0, is a local question for the étale topology on \(Y\). In particular, if \(G\) satisfies (6.3.21.1), the problem 6.3.24.0 admits one and only one solution.
Suppose now that \(G\) satisfies:
(6.3.24.1) For every integer \(n\) and for every diagram of affine \(S\)-schemes
\[\xymatrix@C=2em@R=2em{ X \ar[rr]^{u} \ar[dr]_{f} & & Y \ar[dl]^{g} \\ & T & }\]

with \(f\) and \(g\) flat of finite presentation and \(u\) finite locally free surjective, the truncated semi-simplicial scheme \((\operatorname{Sym}^n_T((X/Y)^{k+1}))_{0 \leq k \leq 2}\), augmented to \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Y)\), is of descent (GIRAUD [1]) for the category of \(G\)-torsors.

6.3.24.1 bis. One deduces in a standard way from 6.3.23 that condition (6.3.24.1) implies the analogous condition, where one assumes only \(f\) and \(g\) flat of finite presentation and quasi-projective and \(u\) flat surjective. Indeed, locally for the étale topology, \(u\) admits finite locally free quasi-sections, and one concludes by 6.3.23 and GIRAUD [1] applied to a diagram forming a square of descent data.

Given a \(G_Y\)-torsor \(K\) on a quasi-projective \(T\)-scheme \(Y\) flat of finite presentation, there exists by definition a faithfully flat morphism of finite presentation \(u : X \longrightarrow Y\) such that \(u^*K\) is trivial. If \(u_i\) denotes the projection of \((X/Y)^{i+1}\) onto \(Y\) (\(i \geq 0\)), the torsors \((u_i^*K)_n\) (6.3.22.1) on the schemes \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T((X/Y)^{i+1})\) form a descent datum (\(i=0,1,2\)) on this semi-simplicial scheme augmented to \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Y)\). Suppose that \(G\) satisfies the condition:
(6.3.24.2) The descent data constructed above are all effective (cf. 6.3.24.1).
Then we shall denote by \(K_n\) the torsor on \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(Y)\) (determined up to unique isomorphism) defined by this descent datum.
6.3.25. Suppose that \(G\) satisfies (6.3.21.1) or the conditions (6.3.24.1) (6.3.24.2). We leave to the reader the task of giving a meaning to the following list of formulae and of verifying it:
6.3.25.1. Base change. Let there be a commutative square
\[\xymatrix@C=2.4em@R=2em{ X' \ar[r]^{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^{f} \\ T' \ar[r]_{g} & T }\]
Let us denote by \(g'_n\) the arrow from \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_{T'}(X')\) to \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\). For \(K\) a torsor under \(G\) on \(X\), we have
\[g'^*_n K_n \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} (g'^*K)_n \, .\]
Let now \(f : X \longrightarrow T\) and \(K\) a \(G_X\)-torsor on \(X\).
6.3.25.2. Change of group. Let \(r : G_1 \longrightarrow G_2\) be a morphism between groups both satisfying (6.3.21.1) or (6.3.24.1), (6.3.24.2). We have
\[r(K_n) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} r(K)_n \, .\]
6.3.25.3. Additivity in \(K\): We have
\[(K' + K'')_n \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} K'_n + K''_n \, .\]
6.3.25.4. Additivity in \(n\). Let \(n_1\) and \(n_2\) be two integers, \(n = n_1+n_2\) and
\[d : \operatorname{Sym}^{n_1}_T(X) \times_T \operatorname{Sym}^{n_2}_T(X) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\]
the canonical arrow; we then have
\[d^*K_n \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \operatorname{pr}_1^* K_{n_1} + \operatorname{pr}_2^* K_{n_2} \, .\]

6.3.25.5. Multiplicativity in \(n\). Let \(n\) and \(m\) be two integers and \(\alpha\) the canonical arrow from \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(\operatorname{Sym}^m_T(X))\) to \(\operatorname{Sym}^{nm}_T(X)\) (cf. 6.3.3). We have
\[\alpha^*(K_{nm}) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} (K_m)_n \, .\]

6.3.26. Suppose that \(G\) satisfies (6.3.21.1) or (6.3.24.1), (6.3.24.2). If \(f : X \longrightarrow T\) is a finite locally free morphism of rank \(n\) between \(S\)-schemes, if \(t\) is the section (6.3.4.2) of \(\operatorname{Sym}^n_T(X)\), and if \(K\) is a \(G_X\)-torsor on \(X\), one defines a \(G_T\)-torsor \(\operatorname{Tr}_f(K)\) on \(T\) by the formula
\[(6.3.26.1) \qquad \operatorname{Tr}_f(K) = t^*(K_n) \, .\]

If \(f\) is finite locally free, one defines \(\operatorname{Tr}_f(K)\), locally on \(T\), by the same formula. This definition, via a canonical and functorial isomorphism, is equivalent to definition 6.3.21 in their common domain of validity (definition 6.3.21 providing a solution to the descent problem posed). One deduces at once from (6.3.25.1), (6.3.25.2) and (6.3.25.3) that the functor \(\operatorname{Tr}_f\) is compatible with base changes \(T' \longrightarrow T\), compatible with changes of group \(r : G_1 \longrightarrow G_2\), compatible with the addition of torsors.
The commutativity of the outer boundary of diagram (6.3.15.2), together with (6.3.25.1) (6.3.25.4), provides a compatibility with the composition of morphisms:
\[\operatorname{Tr}_{fg}(K) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \operatorname{Tr}_f(\operatorname{Tr}_g(K)) \, .\]
6.3.27. In the particular case of relative curves, we moreover have:

blocks.title: Construction
blocks.html:
Construction 6.3.27.1

If \(f : X \longrightarrow S\) is a smooth quasi-projective curve over \(S\), \(D_1\) and \(D_2\) two relative divisors finite over \(S\) and \(K\) a \(G\)-torsor on \(X\), then, setting \(\operatorname{Tr}_{D/S}(K) = \operatorname{Tr}_{D/S}(K|D)\), we have a canonical isomorphism

\[\operatorname{Tr}_{D_1+D_2}(K) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \operatorname{Tr}_{D_1}(K) + \operatorname{Tr}_{D_2}(K) \, .\]
This isomorphism follows at once from the isomorphism (6.3.25.4) and from 6.3.9.1. Finally, the arguments of 6.3.19 again yield:

blocks.title: Construction
blocks.html:
Construction 6.3.27.2

Let there be a commutative diagram

\[\xymatrix@C=2em@R=2em{ X \ar[rr]^{u} \ar[dr]_{p} & & Y \ar[dl]^{q} \\ & S & }\]

in which \(X\) and \(Y\) are smooth quasi-projective curves over \(S\) and \(u\) a quasi-finite morphism.

(i) If \(D\) is a divisor on \(X\) finite over \(S\) and \(K\) a torsor under \(G\) on \(Y\), we have (cf. note p.192):

\[\operatorname{Tr}_{D/S}(u^*K) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \operatorname{Tr}_{(u_* D)/S}(K) \, .\]

(ii) If \(E\) is a divisor on \(Y\) finite over \(S\), \(K\) a torsor under \(G\) on \(X\) and if \(u\) is finite, we have

\[\operatorname{Tr}_{E/S}(\operatorname{Tr}_{X/Y}(K)) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \operatorname{Tr}_{u^*E/S}(K) \, .\]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.28

Let \(A\) and \(B\) be two \(R\)-algebras (commutative) and \(u : A \longrightarrow B\) a homomorphism which makes \(B\) an \(A\)-module locally free of finite type and faithful. Then the semi-simplicial complex of algebras \((\mathrm{TS}^n_R(\otimes_A^{k+1} B))_{k \geq 0}\) is, as a \(\mathrm{TS}^n_R(A)\)-semi-simplicial differential module, a split resolution of \(\mathrm{TS}^n_R(A)\).

Proof. The complex of modules associated with the semi-simplicial module \(\mathrm{TS}^n_R(\otimes_A^{k+1} B)\) depends only on the \(A\)-module \(B\), equipped with a module homomorphism \(u : A \longrightarrow B\). As an \(A\)-module, \(B\) can be written \(B = A \oplus L\), and this allows one to make explicit a homotopy operator.
Let us recall that:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.29

Let \(A\) be a ring, \(B^*\) a co-semi-simplicial \(A\)-algebra, and \(c : A \longrightarrow B^*\) the structural morphism. For the inverse image functor of modules (= extension of scalars) \(\varepsilon^*\) to be faithful (resp. fully faithful) it suffices that the sequence of \(A\)-modules

\[0 \longrightarrow A \longrightarrow B^0\]

(resp. \(0 \longrightarrow A \longrightarrow B^0 \xrightarrow{j_0 - j_1} B^1\))

be exact, and remain so after tensoring by any \(A\)-module.
The proof is trivial and left to the reader.
One deduces in a standard way from (6.3.28) (6.3.29) the

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 6.3.30

Condition (6.3.24.1) is satisfied by every affine group \(G\).
(Use that a torsor under \(G\) is representable by an affine scheme over \(T\).)

It should not be difficult to extend 6.3.30 to every group \(G\) representable by an algebraic space(∗). I conjecture that condition (6.3.24.2) is satisfied by every group representable by an algebraic space, and flat. We have the hoax-like statement:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.3.31

Let there be an exact sequence over \(S\)

\[0 \longrightarrow G \xrightarrow{\;r\;} G' \xrightarrow{\;u\;} H \longrightarrow 0 \, .\]
